lambda-concurrency-cut-after-deploy.cause: Reserved concurrency was cut to 5 at 07:47:55 (PutFunctionConcurrency); requests beyond 5 in flight are throttled. The 07:41 deploy of version 58 is a red herring: no errors, normal durations.

lambda-retry-storm-partner-outage.cause: The partner rates API started failing at 07:52 (503s, now 429s); the function, reconfigured at 06:12 to retry 10 times with no backoff at 200 concurrent executions, turns that outage into a retry storm that keeps the partner rate-limiting. Stop the consumer (messages wait in SQS) and hand to a person.

lambda-errors-logs-unreadable.cause: Unknown: invocations end at the 60 s timeout and fail, nothing changed on the function, but its log group could not be read (AccessDenied on FilterLogEvents and StartQuery), so the reason is not in the evidence.

lambda-batch-duration-threshold.cause: The daily reconcile batch ran for 44 s, finished and errored nowhere; its timeout is 900 s. The alarm's 30 s threshold is set too low for this function.

vpc-dns-resolution-lambda.cause: From about 07:53 every name lookup inside the function's VPC fails (the private Aurora endpoint, DynamoDB and Secrets Manager alike) while the function itself did not change: VPC DNS resolution broke (a VPC-level DNS change), not the code or any one dependency.

ecs-fargate-memory-cut-oom.cause: Task definition revision 19 (same image as 18, deployed 07:38) gives the container 512 MiB instead of 1024; the service runs out of heap while warming its cache and its new tasks die. Roll back to :18.

ecs-ec2-clock-skew-sigv4.cause: The container instance ip-10-0-21-77's clock runs about 6 minutes behind: AWS rejects its tasks' SigV4 requests (Signature expired), their readiness checks fail and ECS keeps replacing them on the same host, while tasks on ip-10-0-22-14 are healthy. A person must drain the instance or fix its time sync.
cause_evidence: Signature expired: 20261010T074620Z is now earlier than 20261010T074719Z

ecs-crash-deploy-unprovable.cause: New tasks crash on start (missing module) after an UpdateService at 07:44, which looks like a bad deploy, but WARDEN's reader was denied DescribeTaskDefinition, so no deploy record, previous revision or task role was read: the rollback target is unproven. A person decides.

codepipeline-redeploy-loop-ecs.cause: CodePipeline has pushed api 7.3.0 three times since 07:04 (task definitions up to :44); each time the new tasks fail on a missing API_SIGNING_KEY_ARN and the ECS circuit breaker rolls the service back to :41. The service is already on the good revision; stop further deploys while a person fixes the pipeline.

iam-policy-edit-accessdenied.cause: From 07:52 the function's execution role no longer allows dynamodb:PutItem on the orders table (no identity-based policy allows it): its IAM policy was edited. The function itself did not change.
cause_evidence: is not authorized to perform: dynamodb:PutItem
because no identity-based policy allows the dynamodb:PutItem action

eks-crashloop-surge-pending.cause: cart 3.1.0 (rollout revision 9 at 07:46) panics at start on a missing CART_REDIS_ADDR. The FailedScheduling (Insufficient cpu) is the rollout's surge pod waiting for room - a side effect, not the cause; adding capacity would only add crashing pods. Roll back to revision 8.

rds-storage-full-replication-slot.cause: An inactive replication slot retains about 57 GiB of WAL (ReplicationSlotDiskUsage, OldestReplicationSlotLag), filling the 100 GiB volume, which has no storage autoscaling; the instance is storage-full. The 05:02 ModifyDBInstance by terraform is a red herring.

aurora-idle-in-transaction-replica-lag.cause: warden-dev-fulfilment holds ~1,388 sessions idle in transaction (some for 30 minutes), exhausting the writer's connections (1702/1800). The replica lag from a 21-minute analytics query on the reader is a separate, minor issue, not the cause.

dynamodb-provisioned-write-throttle.cause: An UpdateTable by the FinOps automation at 06:31 left the table provisioned at 50 WCU with no headroom; the morning write load consumes all 50 WCU and ~18k writes are throttled.

sqs-fifo-poison-message.cause: One malformed message (amount '12,50', group acct-20417, received ~200 times) fails on every delivery; the FIFO batch processor stops at it and returns the rest, so the queue makes no progress (5,120 waiting, oldest ~100 minutes). The queue has no dead-letter queue, so it loops forever. Not a code change; a person must remove or dead-letter that one message.
cause_evidence: FIFO batch stopped at first failure

sqs-dlq-broken-consumer.cause: Version 15 (07:33) expects the payment amount as a string and rejects every message whose amount is an integer; the messages exhaust their receives and land in the DLQ. Roll back to 14; redriving now would only fail them again.
cause_evidence: Input should be a valid string

sqs-dlq-redrive-after-rollback.cause: Version 22 (07:22) failed on messages without carrier_code and dead-lettered 412 shipments; on-call moved the live alias back to 21 at 07:51 and processing has succeeded since. What remains is to redrive the DLQ to the source queue.

sns-queue-policy-denies-topic.cause: The fulfilment queue's access policy no longer lets the topic send to it (the analytics queue's still does), so every delivery to that subscription fails; nothing changed on the topic itself.

eventbridge-rule-disabled-by-apply.cause: A terraform apply at 07:12 rewrote the rule (PutRule) with State DISABLED; the 15-minute settlement poll has not fired since. Turn the rule back on.

scheduler-daily-burst-throttle.cause: The daily 08:00 burst of ~2,400 reminder schedules briefly exceeds the target's capacity; Scheduler retries the throttled invocations and none is dropped or dead-lettered. An alarm on any throttled target error is too strict.

stepfunctions-new-version-failing.cause: A new state machine definition was published and the alias moved to it at 07:36; since then almost every execution fails within about a second. Return the alias to the previous version.

kinesis-write-throttle-consumer-lag.cause: Two limits of a 2-shard provisioned stream at once: producers write ~2,800 records/s and ~2 MiB/s (limits 2,000/s and 2 MiB/s) and are throttled, and the shared-throughput readers exceed the read limit, so the consumers are 90 minutes behind. More shards fixes both.

apigw-rest-integration-timeout.cause: Failing requests wait the full 29 s integration timeout: the stage's backend integration stopped answering in time while nothing on the API changed. The backend is not named in the evidence; a person must find it. (Count and 4XXError read as 1 because their Maximum is per request - not a signal.)

apigw-http-5xx-reads-throttled.cause: Unknown: the HTTP API returns 5xx, but its other metrics (latency, integration latency) and its change history could not be read (both reads throttled), so neither a backend failure nor a change can be established.

alb-single-az-impairment.cause: All three targets in ap-south-1a time out on health checks while ap-south-1b and 1c are fully healthy and nothing changed: an Availability Zone impairment. Zonal shift is enabled; shift traffic away from ap-south-1a.

nlb-instance-refresh-flap.cause: An Auto Scaling instance refresh is rolling instances through the target group one at a time (the Auto Scaling service role deregisters and registers targets every few minutes); a just-registered target counts as unhealthy until it passes 3 checks. An alarm on one unhealthy host for one minute is too sensitive.

elasticache-evictions-no-ttl.cause: The session cache node is full (memory 99%) and evicting live sessions; nothing ever expires (Reclaimed 0), so keys are written without a TTL and a small node fills up. Short term more memory, long term TTLs - a person's call; flushing would log every user out.

memorydb-service-update.cause: Platform-ops applied a service update at 07:30 (BatchUpdateCluster); MemoryDB is patching the nodes one by one, the node failed over and its connections dropped briefly before clients reconnected (240 new connections). Planned maintenance; nothing to change.

s3-bucket-policy-403.cause: The security baseline automation replaced the bucket policy at 07:51 (PutBucketPolicy) and requests that used to be allowed are now refused (4xx from 07:52). The application did not change.

cloudfront-alarm-other-region.cause: Unknown. CloudFront publishes its metrics, and so keeps this alarm, in us-east-1; WARDEN read the environment's own region, found no such alarm and read nothing else about the distribution.
cause_evidence: no metric alarm by that name

route53-alarm-other-region.cause: Unknown. Route 53 health-check metrics and alarms exist only in us-east-1; WARDEN looked in the environment's region, found no alarm, and has no reader for the health check itself, so no evidence was read at all.
cause_evidence: no metric alarm by that name

asg-scheduled-scale-in.cause: A scheduled action (created by terraform at 05:10) took the group from 6 to its 3-instance minimum at 08:00; all 3 remaining instances are healthy. The alarm's threshold (fewer than 4 in service) sits above the group's own minimum.

efs-burst-credits-exhausted.cause: The 200 GiB file system in bursting mode has used up its burst credits; its throughput is held to the 10 MiB/s baseline and clients stall. Changing the throughput mode is a person's decision; more clients would drain it further.

opensearch-flood-stage-write-block.cause: The data nodes' disks reached the flood-stage watermark (the emptiest node has ~4.3 GB of 100 GB free), so OpenSearch made the indices read-only and blocks writes. Needs more storage or data deleted.

msk-rolling-maintenance.cause: MSK is applying a rolling broker update (cluster State MAINTENANCE): broker 2's partitions are under-replicated while it restarts, none below min ISR. AWS-run maintenance; nothing to change.

mq-no-consumers-memory-alarm.cause: No consumer has been attached for the whole window (ConsumerCount 0, AckRate 0) while publishers keep publishing; 4.2 M messages pile up and memory reaches the high watermark, which blocks publishers. The consumers must be fixed by a person; restarting a single-instance broker risks the backlog.

glue-job-failing-after-update.cause: The FinOps automation updated the job at 04:48 (UpdateJob); the hourly runs since then (05:00, 06:00, 07:00) are the 3 failed runs of the last 10. Return the job to its previous definition, or a person decides.

athena-reservation-saturated.cause: All 24 DPUs of the workgroup's capacity reservation have been in use for 30 straight minutes with no change to the workgroup: a runaway query is holding the reservation and everything else queues behind it.

secretsmanager-rotation-half-done.cause: Rotation of warden-dev-orders-db-app is half done: setSecret changed app_user's password in the database, but finishSecret is denied UpdateSecretVersionStage, so AWSCURRENT still holds the old password. Existing connections keep working; every new login with the current secret will fail. A person must finish or undo the rotation.
cause_evidence: setSecret: Successfully set password for user app_user

kms-key-pending-deletion.cause: The KMS key that encrypts the statements is scheduled for deletion (pending deletion), so every Decrypt fails; the function did not change. Cancelling the key deletion is a person's urgent decision.

acm-imported-cert-expiring.cause: An imported certificate, which ACM cannot renew, used by 2 resources expires on 2026-10-16; someone must obtain and import a renewed certificate before then.

appconfig-flag-flip-code-path.cause: AppConfig deployment 23 (configuration version 17, completed 07:54:40) turned on tax_engine_v2; the v2 code path has no tax table for some jurisdictions (IN-KA) and fails. No code changed. Revert the configuration.

appconfig-auto-rolled-back.cause: AppConfig deployment 9 (configuration version 12) turned on ranking_v3, errors rose, and AppConfig itself rolled the deployment back when this alarm fired; the function picked up the previous configuration (11) at 08:01 and has served without errors since. Nothing left to change; the flag's owner should look.

cognito-signin-throttle-after-client-cha.cause: The app-client update at 06:41 (UpdateUserPoolClient) shortened refresh-token validity; tokens issued since stop refreshing after an hour, so from ~07:40 clients fall back to full sign-in and exceed the pool's sign-in rate quota. (Sibling counts read 1 because their Maximum is per request - not a signal.)

waf-bot-flood-blocked.cause: A request flood (~184k in 5 minutes) is being blocked by the web ACL while allowed traffic stays at its usual ~2.4k per minute and the ACL did not change: WAF is doing its job. Nothing to change.

nat-gateway-port-exhaustion.cause: About 55,000 simultaneous connections through the NAT gateway exhaust the source ports of its single public IP towards one destination; new connections fail with port-allocation errors. A person must find the client opening them or add addresses to the gateway; more clients would make it worse.

vpc-sg-quarantine-ec2.cause: At 07:56 the automated security responder changed the instance's security groups (ModifyInstanceAttribute) - a quarantine - and its inbound traffic stopped; the instance itself is healthy. This may be a deliberate security isolation: a person must decide, and undoing it automatically could release a compromised host.

servicequotas-lambda-concurrency.cause: Account-wide Lambda concurrency is at 968, close to the account quota (1,000 by default here); functions without reserved concurrency will start to throttle. Needs a quota increase or a person to find the consumer; reserving more concurrency for one function would starve the rest.
